## Table 1: How many exoplanets are in the habitable zone?

```{r table1}
hz_summary <- summarize_habitable_zone(usablePlanets)
knitr::kable(hz_summary, caption = "Confirmed exoplanets by habitable-zone class")
```

```{r numbers, include=FALSE}
n_total <- nrow(usablePlanets)
n_hz    <- hz_summary$n[hz_summary$class == "Habitable zone"]
pct_hz  <- hz_summary$pct_of_known[hz_summary$class == "Habitable zone"]
pct_hot <- hz_summary$pct_of_known[hz_summary$class == "Too hot"]
```

```{r chart1}
counts <- setNames(hz_summary$n, hz_summary$class)
bp <- barplot(counts,
              col  = c("steelblue", "forestgreen", "firebrick", "grey70"),
              ylim = c(0, max(counts) * 1.15),
              ylab = "Number of planets",
              main = "Confirmed exoplanets by habitable-zone class")
text(bp, counts, labels = counts, pos = 3)
```

Out of 6451 confirmed exoplanets, 290 are in the habitable zone. Which is 5.0% of the planets whose insolation is known. Most planets (87.9%) are too hot because they orbit too close to their star for them to be hospitable. 

## Table 2: Which HZ planets are also Earth-sized?

```{r table2}
earth_like    <- size_energy_comparisons(usablePlanets)
hz_candidates <- usablePlanets[earth_like,
                               c("pl_name", "pl_insol", "pl_rade", "pl_eqt", "st_teff")]
hz_candidates <- hz_candidates[order(abs(hz_candidates$pl_insol - 1)), ]
rownames(hz_candidates) <- NULL
knitr::kable(hz_candidates, digits = 2,
             caption = "Earth-sized planets in the habitable zone")
```

Only 27 planets are both in the habitable zone and about the size of Earth. They are listed from most to least Earth-like insolation. All of them orbit stars cooler than the Sun (5772 K): the hottest host star in the table is 4925 K.

### Numerical summary

```{r num-summary}
num_summary <- numeric_summary(usablePlanets,
                               c("pl_insol", "pl_orbsmax", "pl_rade",
                                 "pl_bmasse", "pl_eqt", "st_teff"))
knitr::kable(num_summary, digits = 2,
             caption = "Numerical summary of the main variables")
```

Insolation, orbital distance, radius and mass are strongly right-skewed, the mean is much larger than the median. For example, the median insolation is 66.7 times Earth’s, but the mean is 531.9 because of a few extremely hot planets. 

### Histogram of insolation

```{r hist}
plot_insolation_histogram(usablePlanets)
```

Most planets receive 10 to 1000 times the energy Earth does, far off to the right of the habitable zone, shown by the green marker. Earth sits within the distribution.

### Density plot of planet size

```{r density}
plot_radius_density(usablePlanets)
```

The dashed lines mark the Earth-size range (0.5 to 1.5 Earth radii). Planets that are too hot are mostly 1 to 4 Earth radii, while HZ and too-cold planets are more often giants of around 10 Earth radii.


```{r save-figures}
save_plot_png(plot_insolation_histogram,   usablePlanets, "hist_insolation.png")
save_plot_png(plot_radius_density,         usablePlanets, "density_radius.png")
```

```{r save}
write.csv(hz_summary,    "hz_summary.csv",    row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(hz_candidates, "hz_candidates.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(num_summary,   "numeric_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE)
save(hz_summary, hz_candidates, solar, num_summary,
     file = "17_AnalysisResults.RData")
```
